extracted.intended_audience: depositors of microorganisms for patent purposes; international depositary authorities (IDAs); industrial property offices; patent practitioners and administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory rules for making, accepting, storing, converting, transferring and furnishing samples of microorganism deposits under the Budapest Treaty, including IDA and national industrial property office procedures. Covers required statements, forms, viability testing, fees, language, duration and contingency arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure sufficiency and deposit necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: For adequate disclosure the invention must be described so a person skilled in the art can repeat it; where an invention involves a new microorganism not available to the public, written description alone may be insufficient and deposit of the microorganism should supplement the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: isolates from soil or organisms changed by mutation/selection may be impossible to describe reproducibly in writing; many national offices require or recommend deposit to ensure repeatability and public availability at the appropriate stage in patent procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of single deposit by Contracting States (IDA principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit made with any international depositary authority (IDA) is to be recognized as sufficient for patent procedure by all States party to the Treaty (and by intergovernmental organizations that have filed declarations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to avoid multiple deposits in different countries; IDAs are nominated by Contracting States which furnish assurances of compliance with Treaty requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA nomination and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA must be formally nominated by the Contracting State on whose territory it is located and that State must furnish solemn assurances that the collection complies and will continue to comply with Treaty and Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key assurances include: availability on same terms to any depositor, storage for the full Treaty-specified period, and furnishing samples only to those entitled to receive them; intergovernmental organizations may furnish similar assurances for collections in member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage duration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited microorganisms must be stored for at least 30 years or five years after the most recent request for a sample, whichever is later (Rule reference in Regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDA must keep microorganism viable and uncontaminated throughout the required storage period; deposits made under Treaty cannot be cancelled during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples — who and when
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples may be furnished at any time to the depositor, to anyone having the depositor’s written authorization, and to any 'interested' industrial property office (i.e., one dealing with a relevant patent application and providing a declaration to the IDA). Other cases are governed by national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because IDAs may not know national laws, third-party requests generally must be made on a form with certification by the relevant industrial property office; alternatively, industrial property offices may notify IDAs of accession numbers of microorganisms referred to in published patents thereby making them publicly available without individual certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard and contingency provisions for deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs must have the expertise and facilities to keep deposits viable and uncontaminated; if an IDA is unable to furnish samples for any reason, a new deposit can be made and may benefit from the date of the original deposit; if an IDA ceases to function, deposits can be transferred to another IDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions guard against loss/non-availability of microorganisms and maintain the legal and practical integrity of deposits for patent purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and interpretation of 'microorganism'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treaty does not define 'microorganism' narrowly; the term is to be interpreted broadly so that entities for which deposit is necessary for disclosure (e.g., tissue cultures, plasmids) may be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether something is treated as a microorganism depends less on strict taxonomy and more on whether deposit is necessary for disclosure and whether an IDA will accept it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of depositor's written statement (Rule 6.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The microorganism transmitted must be accompanied by a written signed statement containing: (i) indication the deposit is under the Treaty and undertaking not to withdraw it for the period specified in Rule 9.1; (ii) name and address of depositor; (iii) details of conditions necessary for cultivation, storage and viability testing and, for mixtures, descriptions of components and at least one method to check their presence; (iv) an identification reference given by the depositor; (v) indication of any properties dangerous to health/environment or a statement that none are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory and the IDA must ask the depositor to comply before accepting the deposit (Rule 6.4(b)); the 'identification reference' can be a strain designation, lab code or name, not necessarily a taxonomic identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional scientific description / taxonomic designation (Rule 6.1(b) and Rule 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended (but not mandatory) that the depositor's written statement contain a scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation; such information may be provided later and amended under Rule 8.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later communications must be signed and include depositor name/address, accession number, the scientific description/designation, and in case of amendment the preceding description; the IDA must, on request, provide an attestation with the information and date received (Rule 8.2) and may charge a fee (Rule 12.1(a)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA permitted administrative and technical requirements (Rule 6.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA may require: (i) that the microorganism be deposited in the form and quantity necessary for the Treaty (e.g., agar slants, lyophilised, minimum titre, replicates); (ii) that an accession/admin form of the authority be furnished; (iii) that the written statement be in the language(s) specified by the authority (including official language(s)); (iv) that the storage fee be paid; (v) that, to the extent permitted by law, the depositor enter into a contract defining liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IDA may apply its normal in-house administrative/technical processing requirements but must inform the International Bureau of WIPO of any such requirements (Rule 6.3(b)); depositor must comply to ensure acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement for submissions to IDA
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA may ask that the written statement (or certain communications) be drafted in the language(s) specified by the authority, which must at least include the official language(s) indicated under Rule 3.1(b)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a Japanese IDA may require information in Japanese; language rules are limited to what's specified by the nominating State or organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage fee — single payment covering whole storage duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA may charge the depositor a fee for storage in accordance with the Treaty; that fee must cover the whole duration of storage and therefore be a once-and-for-all payment (Rule 12.1(a)(i) and Rule 12.1(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IDA may require payment of this fee as a condition for acceptance under Rule 6.3(a)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted grounds for refusal to accept a deposit (Rule 6.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA shall refuse to accept a microorganism only where: (i) the microorganism is not of a kind the IDA has assured it will accept; (ii) properties are so exceptional the IDA is technically unable to perform required tasks; (iii) the deposit is received in a condition indicating the microorganism is missing or otherwise scientifically unacceptable (e.g., broken receptacle, contamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the only legitimate grounds for refusal aside from continued non-compliance by depositor; improper refusal could lead to loss of IDA status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance procedure and date of deposit (Rule 6.4(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to permitted refusal, the IDA shall accept the microorganism when all requirements of Rule 6.1(a)/6.2(a) and Rule 6.3(a) are complied with; if requirements are not complied with, the IDA must immediately notify the depositor and invite compliance. The date of the original or new deposit is the date on which the microorganism was received by the IDA (with conversion exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal acceptance may be deferred pending compliance without prejudicing the date of deposit (except for conversion cases under Rule 6.4(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of prior non‑Treaty deposits to Budapest deposit (Rule 6.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA may, on the depositor's request and provided all requirements are complied with, consider a microorganism deposited before the IDA acquired its status to have been received for Treaty purposes on the date the IDA acquired IDA status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For some national offices the date recognized may vary (e.g., some may recognize date IDA received microorganism or date of request for conversion); conversion is available only to original depositor or successor in title and some IDAs may refuse conversion of scientific-purpose deposits because of distribution constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of official receipt on international form (Rule 7.1–7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt and acceptance (or conversion), the IDA must notify the depositor by issuing an official receipt on the international form BP/4; the receipt must be signed by an authorized representative and contain required indications per Rule 7.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of prescribed international forms by IDAs is mandatory wherever the Regulations specify such use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing and issuance of viability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA must carry out viability testing and issue a viability statement; for mixed cultures the tests must show viability of all components before a positive viability statement is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for cultivation, storage and testing (provided by depositor) enable the IDA to handle the microorganism correctly; see paragraphs on viability testing for procedural details and form BP/9 for test reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-withdrawal obligation of depositor during prescribed period (Rule 9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositor undertakes not to withdraw the deposit for the period specified in Rule 9.1 (i.e., at least 30 years or five years after the most recent request for a sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deposit made under the Treaty cannot be cancelled during this period either by the depositor or the IDA, regardless of patent grant status or abandonment of applications referring to the deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA notification to WIPO/International Bureau of additional requirements (Rule 6.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDA demands any of the optional administrative/technical requirements permitted under Rule 6.3(a), it must inform the International Bureau of WIPO of such requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This keeps the international community informed of IDA-specific practices that depositors must follow to ensure acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for changing the list of kinds of microorganisms accepted (Rule 3.3 & Rule 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDA wishes to limit or extend the kinds of microorganisms accepted, it must notify the Contracting State/organization under whose assurances it acquired IDA status, which must formally notify the Director General of WIPO; limitations come into effect at earliest three months after notification, extensions immediately after publication by the International Bureau unless a later date is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From acquisition of IDA status the collection is obliged to accept the kinds it specified, subject to permitted limitations/exception grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of improper refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal by an IDA to accept a microorganism other than in the limited circumstances permitted by Rule 6.4(a) is in contravention of its Treaty obligations and could lead to loss of its IDA status (Article 8, Rules 4 and 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs must adhere strictly to permitted grounds for refusal to avoid administrative or legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples — procedures, certification and notification (Rules 11.x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for samples must follow Regulations: IPO requests (Rule 11.1) require a request form and declaration that sample is needed for patent procedure; authorized party requests (Rule 11.2(ii)) require depositor authorization; third-party requests typically require industrial property office certification (Rule 11.3) unless the microorganism has been made available by notification of accession numbers; IDA must notify depositor when sample furnished (Rule 11.4(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed international forms (e.g., BP/10, BP/11, BP/12, BP/13, BP/14) exist for different request/certification scenarios; fees and indications provided by IDA must follow Regulations; health and safety rules apply to handling and shipping samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for making a valid request for a sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must identify accession number, supply appropriate certification or depositor authorization as required by the rule invoked, state that sample and any info will be used only for patent procedure, and may request indication of IDA cultivation/storage conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidance covers obtaining samples with depositor authorization, obtaining with IPO certification, obtaining samples of deposits cited in US patents, obtaining under Rule 11.3(b), and compliance with health and safety requirements; requests are often transmitted via competent industrial property office according to its procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed international forms for deposit, testing and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations prescribe use of specific international forms for receipts, viability test reporting and requests for furnishing samples (e.g., BP/4 for receipt, BP/9 for viability test results, BP/10–BP/14 for various request/certification forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms must be completed in duplicate where indicated; certain boxes must be crossed as applicable; signatures and, where legal entities sign, typewritten names of signatories should accompany signatures; IDAs/IPO must follow the model forms precisely when Regulations require 'international form' use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of deposited microorganisms (when needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDA ceases to function or for other specified reasons, deposits may be transferred to a substitute IDA; obligations of the Contracting State, substitute IDA and rights/position of the depositor are governed by the Treaty and Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer preserves availability and legal status of deposit; procedural details and obligations (e.g., ensuring viability, notification) are specified in the relevant sections of the Guide and Regulations.
